banner: APS INDEX PROBE - NO 3 IN THE CUTOFF - ZERO KNOBS

carriers.why: Closed and odd-dimensional. A chiral APS index needs a boundary or a cylindrical end.
Files give g_C = dr^2 + r^2 g_5 for r>0. That is an open cone with a tip, not a compact manifold with boundary. A cutoff radius is not locked.

operator.bundle_on_disk: unique spin structure of T^{1,1}; cone tangent reduced by Hol=SU(3)
operator.dirac_on_disk: Riemannian Dirac of g5, plus a Module A wall-index rule that the project file says is not ker D_5
operator.aps_cut: not stored. The file uses r=0 and j2=0, not the positive spectrum of a boundary Dirac
operator.star_psi: imposed as j2=0 in is_self_dual. Not derived from a computed kernel

formula.why: The file multiplies chi(S^2)^2/4 by the name C2(3) and by sigma*^2. That product is 1. It is not an integral of the A-hat genus.
formula.eta_why: The file sets eta to 0 because its listed lambda_geometric values are non-negative. That is not eta(0) of D on T^{1,1}.

lattice.j2_zero_source: is_self_dual returns true only when j2 is numerically zero
lattice.finite_list_source: the loop stops at j_max written in the file
lattice.why: A finite half-integer list is not forced by a boundary spectrum on disk. The only source is the lattice written in the Python file.

stability.why: On the j1 values stored in r0_modes.json, the r≠0 branch and the j2≠0 branch of the same sieve do not keep the same zero count. This is sieve arithmetic, not an APS kernel.

rows.claim: Closed T^{1,1} is a legal APS carrier
rows.why: Closed and odd-dimensional. A chiral APS index needs a boundary or a cylindrical end.

rows.claim: Open cone as written is a legal APS carrier
rows.why: Files give g_C = dr^2 + r^2 g_5 for r>0. That is an open cone with a tip, not a compact manifold with boundary. A cutoff radius is not locked.

rows.claim: star Psi = Psi is derived from a kernel
rows.why: imposed as j2=0 in is_self_dual. Not derived from a computed kernel

rows.claim: Named product is an A-hat integral
rows.why: The file multiplies chi(S^2)^2/4 by the name C2(3) and by sigma*^2. That product is 1. It is not an integral of the A-hat genus.

rows.claim: File eta is the eta-invariant of the boundary Dirac
rows.why: The file sets eta to 0 because its listed lambda_geometric values are non-negative. That is not eta(0) of D on T^{1,1}.

rows.claim: Finite j lattice is forced by geometry
rows.why: A finite half-integer list is not forced by a boundary spectrum on disk. The only source is the lattice written in the Python file.

rows.claim: Sieve zero-count is stable under listed discrete branches
rows.why: On the j1 values stored in r0_modes.json, the r≠0 branch and the j2≠0 branch of the same sieve do not keep the same zero count. This is sieve arithmetic, not an APS kernel.

rows.claim: dim ker of a named APS operator is computed
rows.why: No boundary Dirac spectrum is stored, so the kernel dimension is not computed.
